newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission proposes tighter van emission limits.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission proposes tighter van emission limits.

text.p: The European Commission proposed tighter emission standards for light commercial vehicles on Friday which would cut allowed limits for carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons, nitrous oxides and fine soot from 2000.

"The measures now being proposed would be applied to new types of vehicles with effect from 1 January 2000 for vehicles in the lighter class and with effect from 1 January 2001 for other vehicles," the Commission said in a news statement.

Categories affected by the proposal, which requires EU national government and European parliamentary approval for adoption, include car-derived commercial vehicles, vans weighing up to 3.5 tonnes, cars weighing more than 2.5 tonnes, or with more than six seats, and off-road vehicles.
The Commission set further targets for 2005 which would cut polluting emissions by half compared with the year-2000 figures.

"This long-term objective gives the motor vehicle and equipment manufacturers a signal that they should continue with their research and development efforts in the field of environmental technologies," it said.

The measures are part of a package linked to the Commission's so-called auto-oil programme, which has looked at the worst sources of transport-related pollution so as to target more effectively new engine and fuel quality standards for cars, vans and lorries.
